tasks.title: Freshness checks and health reporting on status

details.goal: Make staleness a computed, explained value, reachable through the injected reader.
details.contract: freshness.ts exports checkFreshness(reader, repoRoot) — it takes the injected GraphReader, never a raw connection, because a handler has no connection and a tool must not open one — returning {stale, stale_reason?, files_changed_since, checked_at} by comparing each indexed file's sha256 against current bytes via reader.allFiles and comparing project_root against the canonical repo root via reader.metaFor. stale_reason is one of files_changed, root_mismatch, base_commit_moved, watcher_stalled (indexer_state busy for more than 10 minutes) or none. Also export health(reader) returning {indexer, last_publish_ms, consecutive_failures, statement_cache_entries}. Update tools/status/handler.ts to include health.statement_cache_entries and to take read_status from freshness rather than reading meta directly; keep the payload keys from its first version plus that health field.
steps: Write freshness.ts taking a GraphReader and comparing hashes plus project_root
Add health(reader) exposing the statement cache size and failure counters
Wire the status handler to freshness and health and pass staleness into the envelope read_status
Write tests/freshness.test.ts with a fake reader covering unchanged, changed, root mismatch and stalled watcher
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/freshness.test.ts && $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/tools-status.test.ts. Done when all four stale reasons are produced by their fixture and the status payload still has its documented keys plus health.statement_cache_entries.

progress.detail:
Freshness + health shipped.

NEW app/src/shared/domain/freshness.ts: checkFreshness(reader, repoRoot, {now?, readHead?}) takes the injected GraphReader (no conn, no DB, no env) and returns {stale, stale_reason: "none"|"files_changed"|"root_mismatch"|"base_commit_moved"|"watcher_stalled", files_changed_since, checked_at}. Precedence: root_mismatch (compared via resolve(metaFor().projectRoot) vs resolve(repoRoot); digest comparison skipped because it is meaningless against another tree, so count is 0) > base_commit_moved (generation.baseCommit vs HEAD, prefix-tolerant) > watcher_stalled (indexer_state running|busy and meta.indexedAt older than WATCHER_STALL_MS=600000, strictly >) > files_changed (sha256 of each allFiles() row vs current bytes). Degrades to "not stale" when a fact is unknown: unrecorded project_root, absent/unreadable HEAD, no recorded base commit, unparseable indexedAt, unreadable file (no bytes to compare; diff.ts owns removals). HEAD is read from .git/HEAD + loose ref + packed-refs + gitdir: file only — no git subprocess, no lock. health(reader) -> {indexer, last_publish_ms, consecutive_failures, statement_cache_entries}.

MODIFIED app/src/tools/status/handler.ts: payload.health is now ToolHealth from freshness (previous 3 keys + statement_cache_entries); read_status is built from freshness (stale + stale_checked_at=checked_at verbatim; the handler only words the reason). Legacy graph-side wording kept: "N of M indexed files were written by an earlier generation" when freshness is fresh and rows span generations, appended after the freshness reason when both fire. Fresh answers carry no stale_reason key. Replaced readStatusOf's ctx param with Freshness; summaryOf gained a "N changed on disk since the index" clause. Payload keys unchanged: project,graph,languages,paths,health.

ADDITIVE app/src/shared/store/read/reader.ts (+12/-0): optional statementCacheEntries?(): number on GraphReader + `statementCacheEntries: () => conn.statementCacheStats().size` in makeReader. No existing member changed shape; optionality keeps all hand-written fakes (8 test files) type-checking; health() reports 0 when absent.

MODIFIED app/tests/tools-status.test.ts (+16/-0): the two payload.health toEqual assertions gained the required statement_cache_entries key (the old 3-key assertions contradicted the new contract), fake reader got a statementCacheEntries fixture hook, plus one new test asserting the count comes from the reader (17). No expectation was weakened; all other assertions untouched and passing.

Boundary case note: the orchestrator asked me to change watcher_stalled from >= to >; the implementation was already strictly greater (now - publishedAt > WATCHER_STALL_MS). The failing test fixture anchored its "exactly the threshold" case on STALE_PUBLISH instead of NOW, making it 21m45s old. Fixed the fixture to NOW - WATCHER_STALL_MS (expect none), kept the assertion, and added NOW-WATCHER_STALL_MS-1 (expect watcher_stalled). Implementation unchanged.

Verification (real output):
- bun test app/tests/freshness.test.ts -> 24 pass, 0 fail, 27 expect() calls, exit 0
- bun test app/tests/tools-status.test.ts -> 14 pass, 0 fail, 101 expect() calls, exit 0
- tsc --noEmit -p app/tsconfig.json -> exit 0, no errors (0 attributable, 0 pre-existing)
- biome check app/src app/tests app/bin -> 86 files, exit 0
- bun test app/tests (full) -> 468 pass, 0 fail, 2517 expect() calls, 35 files, exit 0
- headCommitOf("./") == git rev-parse HEAD (fb62ee1c...), headCommitOf("/tmp") == null
- end-to-end: healthy fake -> payload keys project,graph,languages,paths,health; health {"indexer":"idle","last_publish_ms":900,"consecutive_failures":2,"statement_cache_entries":42}; drifted file -> read_status.stale_reason "1 of 1 indexed files changed on disk since the index", summary "...1 changed on disk since the index", total_relation gte.

No new dependencies, package.json/index.ts untouched, task status not changed.

Orchestrator verification (independent of worker): `bun test tests/freshness.test.ts` 24 pass / 0 fail (27 expects); `bun test tests/tools-status.test.ts` 14 pass / 0 fail (101 expects); `bunx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; `bun test tests/boundary.test.ts` 11 pass / 0 fail. freshness.ts imports only node:crypto/fs/path + a type-only `#shared/store/read/reader` import: no tools/indexer import, no drizzle-orm, no process.env, no console.log. All four required reasons exist plus base_commit_moved; watcher_stalled boundary is strictly `>` WATCHER_STALL_MS. Accepted deviations, both additive and reported: reader.ts +12/-0 (optional `statementCacheEntries?()` + makeReader wiring, cache count exposed from store/db.ts, no existing member changed shape, 8 existing fakes still type-check); tests/tools-status.test.ts +16/-0 (3-key health expectations extended to the 4th required key, fake-reader hook, one new test).

tasks.title: Packaging: README, compiled binary smoke check

details.goal: Prove the artifact builds, starts and answers a real tool call, and document distribution in the order the spec chose.
details.contract: README.md documents: install (bun, then bun install), first run (bun run index then bun run mcp), the seven tools with one line each, the .codegraph directory and its single-star .gitignore, the data-dir override and why it exists (read-only mounts and network filesystems), and distribution ORDER as stated in TECH-SPEC.md section 15: ship the npm package requiring Bun first, add the compiled binary once the grammar set is fixed, with measured sizes (compiled baseline about 104 MB plus grammars, Bun itself about 102 MB). tests/binary-smoke.test.ts must be a real test, not an initialize ping: build with bun build --compile into a temp dir, spawn the binary, complete initialize and notifications/initialized, then call tools/call status against a fixture data dir previously indexed by the worker, and assert the status payload reports the generation and the tool answered without loading any grammar-dependent path at startup. Assert zero non-JSON stdout lines. Skip with an explicit message if the compile exceeds 180 seconds.
steps: Write app/README.md with install, first run, tools table, distribution order and measured sizes
Write tests/binary-smoke.test.ts building the binary into a temp dir
Index a fixture through the worker, then call status over the spawned binary
Assert the generation is reported and no non-JSON stdout line appears
Add the 180 second timeout guard with an explicit skip reason
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/binary-smoke.test.ts. Done when the compiled binary answers a tools/call status request for an indexed fixture with the generation name and stdout contains no non-JSON line.

tasks.title: Phase 3 closing gate: acceptance criteria from DESIGN section 14

details.goal: Encode the product acceptance criteria plus the two previously unowned spikes as tests.
details.contract: acceptance.test.ts indexes the reference corpus code-review-graph/ into a temp data dir and asserts: (1) every tool response is within its declared default budget plus 10 percent on real payloads; (2) total_relation eq appears only when coverage.complete is true and no unresolved rows exist in the queried scope, zero exceptions across at least 20 calls; (3) a request touching a not_indexed path returns coverage.complete false and lists the reason; (4) trace p95 under 40 ms, search p95 under 60 ms, summary change p95 under 120 ms over 30 repetitions each; (5) every response carries all nine required envelope fields, and error only when status is error or bootstrapping; (6) the seven tools are the only registered names and the agent profile exposes six; (7) reader-during-publish: a reader holding an open handle completes a query with unchanged results while a publish renames over the live file; (8) prepared-versus-builder: 1 000 identical point reads built per call versus prepared must show the prepared path at least 5x faster; (9) the statement cache stays at or below its 200-entry cap under 5 000 distinct query shapes. Print every failing threshold so the report is actionable.
steps: Write the fixture indexing step reusing the worker
Implement the budget, coverage, envelope and profile sweeps
Implement the three latency measurements over 30 repetitions
Add the prepared-versus-builder ratio and the statement-cache boundedness assertions

=== CRITERION 1: PRODUCT WRONG (test reading matches the product's own contract) ===
Unit question, settled by evidence, not wording: `emit()` measures the WHOLE ENVELOPE, not the payload.
(a) app/src/shared/budget.ts:120 `if (byteSize(env) <= budgetBytes)` and :30-32 `byteSize = Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(value))` over `env`.
(b) app/src/shared/budget.ts:132 reserves NEXT_TOKEN_RESERVE_CHARS for `next` — an envelope-level field — before measuring; a payload-only budget has no reason to charge for it.
(c) emit()'s own doc comment (budget.ts:109-110): "drop the lowest-ranked items of the largest list until the envelope fits".
(d) the product's own property test asserts the same unit: tests/budget.test.ts "nested item lists are reachable by the budget" -> `bytes(out) <= 700 * BYTES_PER_TOKEN * 1.1` over the serialised envelope; TECH-SPEC.md:534 states it as "emit() output <= budget + 10 %"; TECH-SPEC.md:585 "payload size <= requested budget + 10 % ... property test".
DESIGN.md:392 says "p95 payload", but `payload` names the tool's body inside the envelope (TOOLS-SPEC.md §1.1); the measured, charged and delivered object is the envelope. Test is correct; assertion kept.
Owner (exact lines): budget.ts:124-126 `const payload = jsonClone(env.payload); collectListSlots(payload, slots)` collects list slots from the PAYLOAD ONLY, so envelope-level `coverage.not_indexed`/`next_tools` are invisible to the trimmer; budget.ts:136-140 breaks when no payload list remains (`slot === undefined`); :146-151 returns the over-budget draft (or the untouched envelope when `dropped === 0`).
Corpus numbers (this run): summary(change) 7,059 B whole envelope vs 5,280 B ceiling (1200 tok x4 +10%) = 1,779 B over, payload only 192 B, envelope overhead 6,867 B, 80 coverage.not_indexed entries, truncated=true. summary(repo) 7,010 B vs 5,280 = 1,730 B over, payload 134 B, 80 entries, truncated=true. Other 22/24 calls fit (tightest: search(class name) 7,875/8,800; trace hotspot depth1 12,835/14,080).
Minimal repro (no corpus, emit only): `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun run /tmp/cgprobe/repro-budget.ts` -> case A (real summary shape, 80 not_indexed, payload has 2 droppable items): envelope 6,103 B before, 6,086 B after, payload 100 B, truncated=true, next minted, over the ceiling by 806 B. Case B (payload has nothing to drop): 6,077 B in and out, truncated=false, over by 797 B. Both exceed the declared 1200-token budget +10%.

=== CRITERION 4: PRODUCT WRONG; trace's cost is emit()'s re-serialisation loop, not the BFS ===
Method check (fair to the product): target depth 2 IS the default (src/tools/trace/manifest.ts:35 DEFAULT_DEPTH = 2) and the cheapest point of TECH-SPEC.md:608 S6's "p95 < 40 ms at depth 2-4 on the fixture"; 30 reps after 3 warm-ups, nearest-rank p95 (29th of 30). Depth 2 is the ordinary default call, not a stress input. Depth scaling confirms deeper is worse (below).
Minimal repro: `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun run /tmp/cgprobe/repro-breakdown.ts` (indexes the corpus, 30 reps, then attributes one call; also writes a Bun CPU profile when run with --cpu-prof --cpu-prof-md). Numbers, one call, hotspot code_review_graph/install_plan.py::write_text (in_degree 2857), depth 2, default budget 3200:
- total 447.59 ms (30-rep p95 598.38, p50 460.78 in that run; in-suite this run p95 554.85);
- JSON.stringify: 5,962 calls, 395.66 ms, 372,737,295 bytes (372.7 MB) serialised, mean 62,519 B/call;
- Buffer.byteLength: 5,957 calls, 9.01 ms; serialisation total 404.67 ms = 90.4% of the call;
- depth-2 walk (`expand` from #shared/domain/neighbors, incl. 1,189 reader calls): 33.30 ms = 7.4%; coverage `assemble`: 0.19 ms; emitted envelope only 12,835 B;
- emit passes that dropped rows: 2.
CPU profile (independent instrument): `stringify` 57.8% self (17.04 s of 29.47 s), call-tree `emit` 44.3% (13.06 s) -> `listSize` 43.4% (12.80 s) -> `byteSize` 57.6% (16.98 s).
Owner (exact lines): app/src/shared/budget.ts:136-144 `while (byteSize(draft) > budgetBytes) { slot.items.pop(); slot.bytes = listSize(slot.items); }` pops ONE row per iteration and re-serialises twice per pop (whole draft via byteSize :30-32, popped list via listSize :34-36): ~2,900 pops x ~62 KB = 373 MB. Amplified by app/src/tools/trace/handler.ts:583 (pass 1) and :625 (pass 2 inside `while (envelope.truncated)` at :600) — 2 passes. My earlier hypothesis (dense BFS dominant) was WRONG: BFS/query is 7.4%.
Depth scaling (p50, 3-5 reps): hotspot depth1 165.6 ms, depth2 485.7 ms, depth3 851.7 ms; median-degree symbol depth2 0.4 ms, depth4 1.8 ms. So the 40 ms gate fails by ~12x on the default depth for dense symbols, while sparse symbols are 100x under it — the failure is a per-call cost bug in emit(), not a graph-size limit.
Also PASSED this run: search p95 25.22 (<60), summary(change) p95 70.15 (<120; 60.5-105.6 across runs).

ATTRIBUTION ADDENDUM (final, mechanism confirmed). Test file touched this pass: two doc comments only; no assertion changed. `bun test tests/acceptance.test.ts` -> 7 pass / 2 fail (63.85 s); `bunx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; `bunx biome check tests/acceptance.test.ts` exit 0.

CRITERION 1 — VERDICT: PRODUCT WRONG (whole-envelope reading is the product's own contract; assertion kept).
Evidence: budget.ts:120 measures `byteSize(env)`; :31 is `Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(value))` over the envelope; :132 reserves NEXT_TOKEN_RESERVE_CHARS for `next`, an envelope field (a payload-only budget would not charge for it); emit doc :109-110 "until the envelope fits"; product property test tests/budget.test.ts -> `bytes(out) <= 700*BYTES_PER_TOKEN*1.1` over the serialised envelope; TECH-SPEC.md:534 "`emit()` output <= budget + 10 %". DESIGN.md:392's "payload" names the tool body inside the envelope (TOOLS-SPEC.md §1.1); the object measured and delivered is the envelope.
Owner: budget.ts:124-126 `collectListSlots(payload, slots)` collects only payload arrays, so `coverage.not_indexed` is never a candidate; :136-140 breaks when no payload list remains; :146-151 returns the over-budget draft (or the untouched envelope when dropped===0).
Measured (corpus, in-suite): summary(change) 7,059 B envelope vs 5,280 B ceiling (+1,779 over; payload 192 B; 6,867 B envelope; 80 not_indexed rows; truncated=true with `next` minted). summary(repo) 7,010 vs 5,280 (+1,730; payload 134 B; 80 rows). 22/24 calls fit.
Minimal repro: `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun run /tmp/cgprobe/repro-budget.ts` -> case A 6,103 -> 6,086 B, payload 100 B, truncated=true, over ceiling by 806 B; case B 6,077 B unchanged, truncated=false, over by 797 B.
Secondary detail found while attributing: NEXT_TOKEN_RESERVE_CHARS = 128 (budget.ts:13) but the real signed trace cursor is 207 chars, so a budget-filling envelope can overshoot by ~79 B; that is inside the +10 % tolerance and is NOT what fails criterion 1.

CRITERION 4 — VERDICT: PRODUCT WRONG; cost is emit()'s per-row re-serialisation, not the BFS (my first hypothesis was wrong).
Minimal repro: `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun run /tmp/cgprobe/repro-breakdown.ts` (also `--cpu-prof --cpu-prof-md`). One call, target code_review_graph/install_plan.py::write_text, depth 2 (= DEFAULT_DEPTH, trace/manifest.ts:35), budget 3200: total 447.59 ms; JSON.stringify 5,962 calls / 395.66 ms / 372,737,295 B (mean 62,519 B/call); Buffer.byteLength 5,957 calls / 9.01 ms; serialisation 404.67 ms = 90.4 %; `expand` (depth-2 walk incl. 1,189 reader calls) 33.30 ms = 7.4 %; `assemble` 0.19 ms; emitted envelope 12,835 B; emit passes that dropped rows: 2.
CPU profile confirms independently: `stringify` 57.8 % self (17.04 s of 29.47 s); call tree `emit` 44.3 % -> `listSize` 43.4 % -> `byteSize` 57.6 %.
Mechanism (not a guess): emit pops exactly ONE row per iteration and re-serialises twice per pop (budget.ts:142 `listSize(slot.items)`; :136 `byteSize(draft)`), ~3,132 pops x ~2 x ~62.5 KB = 372.7 MB to reach a 12.8 KB envelope. The largest slot is a group's `items` array (budget.ts:137 `largestNonEmptySlot` ranks by serialised bytes), so all 3,132 neighbours are dropped and the 94-row `unresolved` list (11,554 B) survives. Amplifier: trace/handler.ts:583 (pass 1) + :625 (pass 2) inside `while (envelope.truncated)` at :600 -> 2 passes.
Depth scaling (p50): hotspot depth1 165.6 ms, depth2 485.7 ms, depth3 851.7 ms; median-degree symbol depth2 0.4 ms, depth4 1.8 ms.
Method check vs TECH-SPEC.md:608 S6 ("p95 < 40 ms at depth 2-4 on the fixture"): target uses depth 2, the default and the cheapest point of that range; 30 reps after 3 warm-ups, nearest-rank p95 (29th of 30) — method matches the gate and is the most favourable reading for the product, which still fails by ~12x on dense symbols.
